To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mucopeptide isolated from Bacillus lichteniformis contains glutamic acid and diaminopimelate as the amino acids in the peptide backbone, and alanine, N -acetylmuramic and N -acetylglucosamines as the sugar components.

the mucopeptide isolated from the cell walls of Bacillus lichniformis contains d- and l-alanine and that the mucopeptides from both the cell walls of B. subtilis and B. lichenifonnis contain a d-amino acid.

the mucopeptide of the cell wall of B. lichenformis is composed of repeating units in which a peptide of three amino acids, l-alanine, d-alanine and diaminopimelate, is attached to a disaccharide, N-acetylmureic acid, N-acetyl glucosamine, through a glycosidic bond between the carboxyl group of the muramic acid and the amino group of the diaminopimelyl residue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical structure of the cell wall of Bacilhus licheniformis.
the structure of the mucopeptides of B. lichenformis and the mechanism of the lysozyme reaction on this material.
a detailed study of the composition of the mucopeptides of B. lichenformis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mucopeptide from this organism is a polymer of d-glutamic acid, d-glutamine, l-lysine, l-alanine, d-alanine and diaminopimelate linked by peptide bonds and that the amino acids are arranged in the following order: l-lysine-glutamic acid-glutamic acid-lysine-diaminopimelic acid-alanine.

soluble mucopeptide of B. lichenformis is an alternating copolymer of d-glucosamine and d-muramic acid, with a small proportion of d-alanine linked by peptide bonds between the amino group of muramic acid and the free amino groups of alanine.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the mucopeptides from the Gram-positive bacteria is very similar to that of the mucopeptides from Gram-negative bacteria.

the structure of soluble muopeptide from B.licheniformis differs in several respects from that of soluble mucopeptides from other bacterial species, and that the mucopeptide from this organism is not a simple polymer of the repeating unit N-acetylmuratoyl-d-glutaminyl-meso-2,6-diaminoheptanedioic acid.

the cell wall of Bac. licheniforms is very similar to that of Staph. aureus, and the mucopeptide is a linear polymer of alternating residues of N-acetylglucoseaminylmuramic acid, N-acetylmureinylglutamyl, N-acetylglycyl, and diaminopimelyl.
